title: NY State Assembly · District 54
area: Bushwick and East New York in Brooklyn, including Cypress Hills and City Line.

context.text: Open seat, uncontested in the general election. Christian Celeste Tate (D/WFP) defeated incumbent Erik Dilan 61.9%–37.9% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary (a third candidate, Paperboy Prince, withdrew or was disqualified before the primary). Dilan, first elected in 2016, is not on the November ballot. No Republican or other party candidate qualified, so Tate is running unopposed in the general election.

candidates.name: Christian Celeste Tate
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated incumbent Erik Dilan 61.9%–37.9% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary; running unopposed in the general election.

summary.text: Christian Celeste Tate is a community organizer and democratic socialist who won the Democratic and Working Families Party nominations for the open NY State Assembly District 54 seat, defeating incumbent Erik Dilan in the June 2026 primary. He is running unopposed in the November general election.

background.text: Is a member of Brooklyn Community Board 4, NYC-DSA, the East New York Community Land Trust, and New York Communities for Change.

Has organized with neighbors against landlords he describes as among the city's worst, stood with neighbors in court to fight deed theft, and organized campaigns to tax the wealthy, freeze rents, and create a public bank.
Defeated three-term incumbent Erik Dilan and a third candidate, Paperboy Prince (who withdrew before the primary), in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Housing: create a state Social Housing Development Authority to build permanently affordable homes statewide; support tenant organizing through the Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act; expand Good Cause eviction protections; defend rent stabilization; renew the Bushwick/East New York cease-and-desist zone; and tax speculative home flipping.

Immigration: pass "New York for All" to bar state agencies from collaborating with ICE; adopt "Access to Representation" to guarantee immigration lawyers in deportation cases; and pass "Dignity Not Detention" to bar immigration detention facilities from operating in New York.

Public safety: invest in youth programming and workforce development, expand violence interruption programs, and increase access to school counseling, mental healthcare and substance-use treatment, framing these as addressing root causes of crime rather than only responding to it.

positions.summary: Supports creating a state Social Housing Development Authority, passing the Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act, expanding Good Cause eviction protections, and defending rent stabilization.
positions.quote: We will support tenant organizing through the Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act. We will expand Good Cause protections and defend rent stabilization.

positions.summary: Opposes expanded immigration enforcement; supports barring state agencies from cooperating with ICE, guaranteeing immigration lawyers in deportation cases, and prohibiting immigration detention facilities in New York.
positions.quote: We will pass New York for All to prohibit state agencies from collaborating with ICE.

positions.summary: Says his community organizing has included campaigns to "tax the rich", freeze the rent and create a public bank.
In a 2026 Jim Owles Liberal Democratic Club questionnaire, he answered yes when asked if he supports the unrestricted right to reproductive care and abortion.
In a 2026 Jim Owles Liberal Democratic Club questionnaire, he said he supports universal health care and adopting Coverage For All so all New Yorkers have access to health care.
positions.quote: That's why I support universal housing, healthcare, childcare, and dignity.
